question: Who among the following is NOT a Cabinet Minister? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (20/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: Minister of Home Affairs
Minister of External Affairs
Minister of State in the Ministry of Defence
Minister of Law and Justice
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Minister of State in the Ministry of Defence

Explanation:
In India, the Council of Ministers has three levels: Cabinet Minister, Minister of State (Independent Charge), and Minister of State. Cabinet Ministers head important departments and attend Cabinet meetings. Minister of Home Affairs, Minister of External Affairs, Minister of Defence, and Minister of Law and Justice are all Cabinet Ministers. The Minister of State in the Ministry of Defence is not a Cabinet Minister; he works under the Defence Minister. Therefore, the Minister of State in the Ministry of Defence is NOT a Cabinet Minister.

☛ Requirement to become a Cabinet Minister → Must be a member of Parliament
☛ Minister of State (Independent Charge) is equivalent to → Cabinet Minister
☛ Who appoints Cabinet Ministers → President on the recommendation of Prime Minister
☛ Highest level of Council of Ministers in India → Cabinet Minister
☛ Minister of State is responsible to → Cabinet Minister of the concerned department
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन कैबिनेट मंत्री नहीं होता है? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (20/01/2021) Shift 2)
options_hi: गृह मंत्री
विदेश मंत्री
रक्षा मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री
कानून और न्याय मंत्री
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है रक्षा मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री

Explanation:
भारत में मंत्रिपरिषद के तीन स्तर होते हैं: कैबिनेट मंत्री, राज्य मंत्री (स्वतंत्र प्रभार), और राज्य मंत्री। कैबिनेट मंत्री महत्वपूर्ण विभागों के प्रमुख होते हैं और कैबिनेट की बैठकों में भाग लेते हैं। गृह मंत्री, विदेश मंत्री, रक्षा मंत्री और कानून एवं न्याय मंत्री सभी कैबिनेट मंत्री होते हैं। रक्षा मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री कैबिनेट मंत्री नहीं होता, बल्कि वह रक्षा मंत्री के अधीन कार्य करता है। इसलिए, रक्षा मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री कैबिनेट मंत्री नहीं है।

question: In 1930, who organised the Dalits into the Depressed Classes Association and demanded separate electorates for them? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (20/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: Abdul Gaffar Khan
Jawahar Lal Nehru
BR Ambedkar
Mahatma Gandhi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is BR Ambedkar

Explanation:
In 1930, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar organised the Depressed Classes (Dalits) into the Depressed Classes Association to work for their social and political upliftment. He demanded separate electorates for Dalits, arguing that they needed independent political representation due to caste-based discrimination. This demand was a major point of contention with Mahatma Gandhi, who opposed separate electorates fearing division of Hindu society. The issue was resolved in the Poona Pact (1932), where Ambedkar agreed to reserved seats instead of separate electorates. Ambedkar's efforts focused on ensuring Dalits had a voice in the political process and access to education and employment.

☛ Who demanded separate electorates for Dalits in 1930? → BR Ambedkar
☛ When was the Poona Pact signed? → 1932
☛ What was the outcome of the Poona Pact? → Reserved seats for Dalits
☛ Why is BR Ambedkar considered the leader of Dalits? → For his fight for social justice
question_hi: 1930 में, किसने दलितों को दलित वर्ग संघ में संगठित किया और उनके लिए अलग निर्वाचन क्षेत्रों की मांग की? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (20/01/2021) Shift 2)

Explanation:
1930 में, डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर ने दलितों (तत्कालीन 'अछूत') के उत्थान के लिए दलित वर्ग संघ (Depressed Classes Association) की स्थापना की। उन्होंने दलितों के लिए पृथक निर्वाचन क्षेत्र (separate electorates) की मांग रखी ताकि वे अपने प्रतिनिधि स्वयं चुन सकें। यह मांग ब्रिटिश सरकार को प्रस्तुत की गई थी। अंबेडकर का मानना था कि सामाजिक भेदभाव के कारण दलितों को राजनीतिक प्रतिनिधित्व में समान अवसर नहीं मिलता। यह मांग बाद में गांधी और अंबेडकर के बीच पूना समझौते (1932) का आधार बनी, जिसमें पृथक निर्वाचन के बजाय आरक्षित सीटों पर सहमति बनी।

question: Name the writ under which the court orders that the arrested person should be presented before it or can order to set free an arrested person if the manner or grounds of arrest are NOT lawful or satisfactory. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (20/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: Certiorari
Quo Warranto
Habeas corpus
Mandamus
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Habeas Corpus

Explanation:
Habeas Corpus is a crucial writ under which the court orders that an arrested person be brought before it. If the manner or grounds of arrest are found unlawful or unsatisfactory, the court can order the immediate release of the person. This writ protects personal liberty and is also known as the 'Great Writ'. It can be issued by the Supreme Court under Article 32 and by High Courts under Article 226 of the Indian Constitution. The literal meaning of Habeas Corpus is 'you shall have the body'. Its primary purpose is to prevent illegal detention and ensure that no person is deprived of liberty without legal authority. Other writs include Certiorari, Quo Warranto, and Mandamus.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which right does Habeas Corpus protect? → Personal liberty
☛ Under which articles can this writ be issued? → Article 32 and 226
☛ Which courts can issue this writ? → Supreme Court and High Courts
☛ What is the literal meaning of Habeas Corpus? → 'You shall have the body'
☛ Which writ is also called the 'Great Writ'? → Habeas Corpus
question_hi: उस रिट का नाम बताइए जिसके तहत अदालत आदेश देती है कि गिरफ्तार व्यक्ति को उसके सामने पेश किया जाना चाहिए या गिरफ्तारी के तरीके या आधार वैध या संतोषजनक नहीं होने पर गिरफ्तार व्यक्ति को मुक्त करने का आदेश दे सकता है। (RRB NTPC CBT-I (20/01/2021) Shift 2)
options_hi: उत्प्रेषण
अधिकार पृच्छा
बन्दी प्रत्यक्षीकरण
परमादेश
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है बन्दी प्रत्यक्षीकरण

Explanation:
बन्दी प्रत्यक्षीकरण (Habeas Corpus) एक महत्वपूर्ण रिट है जिसके तहत अदालत गिरफ्तार व्यक्ति को अपने सामने पेश करने का आदेश देती है। यदि गिरफ्तारी का आधार या तरीका अवैध या असंतोषजनक पाया जाता है, तो अदालत उसे तुरंत रिहा करने का आदेश दे सकती है। यह रिट व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता की रक्षा करती है और इसे 'बंदी प्रत्यक्षीकरण' या 'प्रत्यक्षीकरण' भी कहा जाता है। यह भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 32 और 226 के तहत उच्चतम न्यायालय और उच्च न्यायालय द्वारा जारी की जा सकती है। इस रिट का उद्देश्य अवैध हिरासत से व्यक्ति को मुक्त कराना है। अन्य रिटों में उत्प्रेषण (Certiorari), अधिकार पृच्छा (Quo Warranto), और परमादेश (Mandamus) शामिल हैं।

question: How many languages are enlisted in the eighth schedule of the Indian Constitution? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (21/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: 25
23
22
21
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 22

Explanation:
The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution originally listed 14 languages, which have been expanded through amendments. Currently, there are 22 languages enlisted. These languages are recognized for official purposes, education, and cultural preservation. The 21st Amendment (1967) added Sindhi; the 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali; and the 92nd Amendment (2003) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali. The Eighth Schedule reflects India's linguistic diversity.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Most recently added languages → Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali (92nd Amendment, 2003)
☛ Sindhi added by which amendment → 21st Amendment, 1967
☛ Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali added by which amendment → 71st Amendment, 1992
☛ Original number of languages in Eighth Schedule → 14

question: Which Indian state was the first to establish the institution of Panchayat raj? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (21/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Punjab
Andhra Pradesh
Rajasthan
Uttar Pradesh
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Rajasthan

Explanation:
India's first Panchayati Raj system was established in Rajasthan on 2 October 1959. It was based on the recommendations of the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee. The then Chief Minister of Rajasthan was Mohan Lal Sukhadia. The system was inaugurated in Nagaur district. Later, Andhra Pradesh adopted it on 11 November 1959. The Panchayati Raj system is a three-tier structure: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, and Zila Parishad. The 73rd Constitutional Amendment in 1992 gave it constitutional status.

☛ Recommending committee → Balwant Rai Mehta, 1957
☛ Inauguration site → Nagaur, Rajasthan
☛ 73rd Amendment → 1992, constitutional status to Panchayats
☛ Three-tier structure → Village, Intermediate, District levels

question: Hindi was declared as the official language of Union under Article _______ of Indian Constitution. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (21/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: 333
334
345
343
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 343

Explanation:
Article 343 of the Indian Constitution declares Hindi in Devanagari script as the official language of the Union. This provision falls under Part XVII (Official Language). Article 343(1) states that the official language of the Union shall be Hindi in Devanagari script. Article 343(2) provided that for a period of 15 years (until 1965), English would continue to be used for official purposes. Article 343(3) empowers Parliament to continue the use of English beyond that period. Article 345 allows states to adopt their own official language, while Articles 333 and 334 deal with reservations for Anglo-Indians and SC/STs.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ What is the script of Hindi as per the Constitution? → Devanagari
☛ Which Part of the Constitution deals with Official Language? → Part XVII
☛ For how many years was English allowed as an additional official language? → 15 years (until 1965)
☛ Which Article allows states to adopt their own official language? → 345
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद _______ के तहत हिंदी को संघ की आधिकारिक भाषा घोषित किया गया था। (RRB NTPC CBT-I (21/01/2021) Shift 1)
options_hi: 333

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है 343

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 343 में हिंदी को देवनागरी लिपि में संघ की आधिकारिक भाषा घोषित किया गया है। यह प्रावधान भाग XVII (राजभाषा) के अंतर्गत आता है। अनुच्छेद 343(1) के अनुसार, संघ की राजभाषा हिंदी और लिपि देवनागरी होगी। अनुच्छेद 343(2) में कहा गया है कि 15 वर्षों तक (1965 तक) अंग्रेजी भी आधिकारिक कार्यों में प्रयोग की जाती रहेगी। अनुच्छेद 343(3) के तहत संसद को अंग्रेजी के प्रयोग को जारी रखने का अधिकार दिया गया। अनुच्छेद 345 राज्यों को अपनी राजभाषा निर्धारित करने की अनुमति देता है, जबकि अनुच्छेद 333 और 334 एंग्लो-इंडियन और SC/ST के आरक्षण से संबंधित हैं।

question: Which one of the following provisions was a part of the Indian Independence Act of 1947? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (21/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: India will be divided into two parts
India will become a part of Britain
All princely states will remain dependent on British
India will become a monarchy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is India will be divided into two parts

Explanation:
The Indian Independence Act of 1947 provided for the partition of India into two independent dominions: India and Pakistan. This Act was passed by the British Parliament on 18 July 1947 and came into effect on 15 August 1947. It ended British rule in India and granted sovereignty to both dominions. The Act also allowed princely states to choose whether to join India or Pakistan. Additionally, it established the position of Governor-General for each dominion and empowered the respective Constituent Assemblies to frame their constitutions. The Act was a key step in the process of decolonization and laid the foundation for independent India and Pakistan.

question: How many parts are there in the Constitution of India as of October 2020? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (21/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: 23
24
22
25
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 25

Explanation:
As of October 2020, the Constitution of India has 25 parts. The number of parts has increased over time through amendments. The original Constitution had 22 parts. After the 73rd and 74th Amendments (1992), Part IX (Panchayats) and Part IXA (Municipalities) were added, making it 24 parts. Subsequently, the 100th Amendment (2015) added Part IVA (Fundamental Duties), raising the total to 25. Currently, the Constitution consists of 25 parts, 448 articles, and 12 schedules. It is important to note that Parts do not include the Preamble or the Schedules.

question: Which amendment in the Constitution of India deals with the abolition of Right to Property as a fundamental right? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (21/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: 40th
44th
42nd
37th
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 44th Amendment

Explanation:
The 44th Amendment to the Constitution of India, enacted in 1978, abolished the Right to Property as a fundamental right. It removed Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31 from the fundamental rights chapter. Instead, it added Article 300A, making the right to property a constitutional right but not a fundamental right. This amendment was passed by the Morarji Desai government to facilitate land reforms and reduce legal hurdles. The 44th Amendment also modified several other provisions, including the powers of the President and the emergency provisions.

question: Which of the following fundamental rights is NOT guaranteed by the Constitution of India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (22/01/2021) Shift 1)

Right to equality
Right to freedom of religion

Solution: Correct Answer is Right to profession

Explanation:
The Constitution of India guarantees Right to equality (Articles 14-18), Right to freedom (Articles 19-22), and Right to freedom of religion (Articles 25-28) as fundamental rights. Article 19(1)(g) provides freedom of trade, business, industry and profession, which is a fundamental right, but it is not specifically titled 'Right to profession'. Therefore, among the given options, 'Right to profession' is not a fundamental right guaranteed by the Constitution.

भारत के संविधान में मौलिक अधिकारों के अंतर्गत समानता का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 14-18), स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 19-22), और धर्म की स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 25-28) स्पष्ट रूप से गारंटीकृत हैं। जबकि व्यवसाय का अधिकार एक मौलिक अधिकार नहीं है, बल्कि यह संविधान के भाग IV में राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्वों के अंतर्गत आता है। अनुच्छेद 19(1)(g) केवल व्यापार, व्यवसाय, उद्योग और पेशे की स्वतंत्रता प्रदान करता है, जो एक मौलिक अधिकार है, लेकिन यह 'व्यवसाय का अधिकार' शीर्षक से नहीं जाना जाता। इसलिए, विकल्पों में से 'व्यवसाय का अधिकार' कोई मौलिक अधिकार नहीं है।

question: ________ of the Indian Constitution deals with the protection of interests of minorities. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (22/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Article 27
Article 29
Article 28
Article 26
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 29

Explanation:
Article 29 of the Indian Constitution deals with the protection of interests of minorities. It falls under Fundamental Rights (Part III) and grants any citizen or group residing in India the right to conserve their language, script, or culture. Under this article, no citizen shall be denied admission into any educational institution maintained or aided by the State on grounds only of religion, race, caste, or language. This article protects the cultural and educational rights of minority communities. It ensures that minorities can preserve their distinct language and culture, thereby maintaining India's diversity. Article 29 is often read with Article 30, which gives minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions. Together, they form the cornerstone of minority rights in India.

☛ Article 29 is part of which Part? → Part III (Fundamental Rights)
☛ What does Article 29(1) provide? → Right of any citizen to conserve their language, script, or culture
☛ What does Article 29(2) say? → No discrimination in admission to state institutions on grounds of religion, race, etc.
☛ Difference between Article 29 and 30? → Article 29 protects cultural rights, Article 30 gives right to establish educational institutions
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान का _________ अल्पसंख्यकों के हितों के संरक्षण से संबंधित है। (RRB NTPC CBT-I (22/01/2021) Shift 1)

question: Which fundamental right is violated if a group of people are NOT given permission to open a Telugu-medium school in Kerala? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (22/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: Right to Equality
Cultural and Educational Rights
Right to Freedom of Religion
Right to Freedom
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Cultural and Educational Rights

Explanation:
The Indian Constitution provides Cultural and Educational Rights to minorities under Articles 29 and 30. Article 29(1) grants any section of citizens the right to conserve their language, script, or culture. Article 30(1) gives religious or linguistic minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. A Telugu-speaking group in Kerala wanting to open a Telugu-medium school falls under this right. Denying permission violates these rights. These rights are specifically designed to protect the language and culture of minorities. Right to Equality, Freedom of Religion, or Right to Freedom are not directly applicable here as the core issue is about educational and cultural preservation.

question: Which Constitutional Amendment led to inclusion of Sikkim in the Indian Union? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (22/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: 34th Amendment
37th Amendment
33rd Amendment
36th Amendment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 36th Amendment

Explanation:
The 36th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1975 led to the inclusion of Sikkim as a full-fledged state of the Indian Union. Prior to this, Sikkim was a protectorate state with special treaty relations with India. This amendment inserted Article 371F into the Constitution, which contains special provisions for Sikkim. The amendment came into effect on 26 April 1975, following a referendum in Sikkim that voted for merger. With this amendment, Sikkim became the 22nd state of India.

question: The ‘Animal Welfare Board of India’ established in the year 1962, under Section 4 of the ‘Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960’, is a statutory advisory body, formed for advising the Government of India, on animal welfare laws, falls under which ministry? options: Ministry of law and justice
Ministry of earth sciences
Ministry of environment and forest and climate change
Ministry of food and agriculture
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ministry of environment and forest and climate change

Explanation:
The Animal Welfare Board of India (AWBI) was established in 1962 under Section 4 of the 'Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960' as a statutory advisory body. Its primary role is to advise the Government of India on animal welfare laws and prevent cruelty to animals. The Board currently functions under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. Initially, it was under the Ministry of Forests and Environment, but later it was brought under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. question: Who was the first Vice-President of India to be elected as President by second preference count of votes in the presidential elections? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (22/01/2021) Shift 2)

Shankar Dayal Sharma

Explanation:
India's fourth President VV Giri (1969-1974) was the first Vice-President to be elected as President by second preference votes. He won the 1969 election against the official Congress candidate Neelam Sanjiva Reddy. Giri, a socialist leader, was also the first full-time Labour Minister of India. Before becoming President, he served as Vice-President (1967-1969). Giri was supported by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, who advocated for a progressive candidate.

question: Kesavananda Bharti Case in 1973 stemmed the question that the Preamble can _______. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (23/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: be changed completely
be amended
not be amended
be separated into sections
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is be amended

Explanation:
The Kesavananda Bharti case (1973) was a landmark judgment in Indian constitutional history. The Supreme Court propounded the 'Basic Structure Doctrine' in this case. According to this doctrine, the Parliament can amend the Constitution but cannot alter its basic structure. The Preamble is considered an integral part of the Constitution. The judgment clarified that the Preamble can be amended, but not completely changed. The 42nd Amendment (1976) added the words 'Socialist, Secular and Integrity' to the Preamble, which was consistent with this doctrine. Thus, the Preamble is amendable, but subject to the basic structure. This case established that the Preamble can be amended but cannot be completely rewritten. The basic structure includes supremacy of the Constitution, democratic governance, federal framework, and judicial review.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Kesavananda Bharti case (1973) → Basic Structure Doctrine was propounded.
☛ Amendment to Preamble → Done by 42nd Amendment (1976).
☛ Elements of Basic Structure → Supremacy of Constitution, Republican form of Government, Federal character, Judicial review.
☛ Berubari Union case (1960) → Preamble was not considered part of the Constitution.
☛ Minerva Mills case (1980) → Reaffirmed the Basic Structure Doctrine.

question: The constitutional head of the Executive of the Union of India is the: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (23/01/2021) Shift 2)

President

He is also the Supreme Commander of the Indian Armed Forces, but his powers as executive head are limited by the Constitution and the advice of the Council of Ministers. question: To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India is a the: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (23/01/2021) Shift 2)
options: army's duty
fundamental duty
fundamental right
legal right
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is fundamental duty

Explanation:
Under Article 51A of Part IVA of the Indian Constitution, fundamental duties list the obligations of citizens. One of these duties is 'to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India'. This duty was added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976. Fundamental duties are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they cannot be enforced by courts, yet they underline citizens' responsibility towards the nation. Initially there were 10 duties, later the 86th Amendment (2002) added an 11th duty. These duties are inspired by the Constitution of Russia (Soviet Union).

भारत के संविधान के भाग IVA में अनुच्छेद 51A के अंतर्गत मौलिक कर्तव्य नागरिकों के कर्तव्यों को सूचीबद्ध करते हैं। इनमें से एक कर्तव्य है 'भारत की संप्रभुता, एकता और अखंडता को बनाए रखना और उसकी रक्षा करना'। यह कर्तव्य 1976 में 42वें संशोधन द्वारा जोड़ा गया था। मौलिक कर्तव्य स्वरूप में गैर-न्यायिक हैं, अर्थात इन्हें अदालत में लागू नहीं किया जा सकता, फिर भी ये नागरिकों की राष्ट्र के प्रति जिम्मेदारी को रेखांकित करते हैं। प्रारंभ में इसमें 10 कर्तव्य थे, बाद में 86वें संशोधन (2002) द्वारा 11वां कर्तव्य जोड़ा गया।
